Subject: Important: Corvane children’s ibuprofen syringe recall — what parents need to do

We know parents are worried about the children’s ibuprofen recall. A dosing syringe that can cause a child to receive twice the intended dose is a serious safety issue. Here is what is affected and what to do now.

CHECK YOUR BOX

Corvane Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL, berry flavour, 120 mL bottle.
Affected lots: CV6114A and CV6114B.
Expiry: 08/2027.

Check the lot number on the bottom of the box first. If you no longer have the box or cannot confirm the lot, bring the bottle and syringe to a pharmacist for help before using them.

WHAT IS WRONG?

The supplied syringe has incorrectly printed volume markings. The numbers show half the actual volume:
• The mark labelled 2.5 mL actually measures 5 mL.
• The mark labelled 5 mL actually measures 10 mL.

Following those markings can therefore give approximately twice the intended dose.

The manufacturer confirms that the medicine itself meets specifications and is not contaminated. These lots are not expired. The recall concerns the supplied dosing syringe, not the liquid. However, the syringe error creates a real overdose risk.

WHAT TO DO NOW

Stop using the syringe supplied with either affected lot. Discard it and use a correctly marked oral dosing syringe. Do not try to compensate by using different markings on the faulty syringe, and do not use a kitchen spoon. A pharmacist can help confirm the correct dose for your child’s weight and this product’s concentration.

IF YOUR CHILD MAY ALREADY HAVE RECEIVED TOO MUCH

If you have any doubt about a dose already given with the affected syringe, call a poison centre now, even if your child seems well. In Ontario, call 1-844-764-7669 (1-844-POISON-X).

Do not give another dose of ibuprofen until the poison centre or a doctor says it is safe. Have the bottle, syringe, your child’s weight, and the amounts and times of doses available if possible.

An individual assessment depends on your child’s weight, how much was given, how many doses they received, and health factors such as kidney problems. We cannot safely assess a child’s overdose risk through Facebook comments.

Call 911 or go to an emergency department immediately if your child is very sleepy or hard to wake, is vomiting blood, is not urinating, or has a seizure. Do not wait for a Facebook reply or for the pharmacy to open.

REPLACEMENT SYRINGES AND REFUNDS

We open today, Monday, November 9, at 9 a.m. Free replacement oral syringes are expected before noon today; they are not yet confirmed as available at opening. They will be available to anyone who needs one, with no receipt required.

You may also return affected product for a full refund. We will have extra opening hours Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., for exchanges.

We received the recall notice November 6 and posted signs November 7. Many over-the-counter purchases do not include customer contact information, so we cannot reach every purchaser directly. Please share this notice so families can check their supplies.

We’re sorry for the worry this has caused families. We’ve put a detailed recall notice on the Cedarbrook Pharmacy page, including affected lots, the syringe error, replacements and refunds.

The affected Corvane lots are CV6114A and CV6114B, exp. 08/2027. The liquid is not contaminated; the supplied syringe markings can cause approximately double the intended dose. Please stop using that syringe.

If you are unsure about any dose already given, call Ontario’s poison centre now at 1-844-764-7669. Do not give more ibuprofen until the poison centre or a doctor says it is safe. For severe symptoms, call 911 or go to emergency rather than waiting for us to open.
